title: Transaction envelope followed by three zero bytes must be refused by the transaction parser
caps_note: An XDR decoding rule (a value is the whole input: stellar-core refuses an envelope with bytes after it), not a CAP.
why: The control for the two members before it: three extra bytes after the 136-byte envelope start a new base64 quantum, so even a parser that counts base64 characters sees unread input and refuses. A reader that refuses this but accepts one or two extra bytes checks consumption in encoded characters, not decoded bytes.
notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/xdr-strict/api-transaction-parse-trailing-bytes.three-bytes-next-quantum.json. Origin: go-stellar-sdk#6039. The envelope is hand-encoded: ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX, an ed25519 source, fee 100, sequence 1, PRECOND_NONE, MEMO_TEXT "xcc", one native payment of 1 XLM, no signatures; 136 bytes. xdr_hex is that envelope followed by three zero bytes. The driver passes the bytes to the SDK the way an application receives an envelope (base64 for go-stellar-sdk's txnbuild.TransactionFromXDR). Expected values were computed from the XDR definitions and the rule cited under related, with an independent encoder; no SDK output was used.
